blocks.summary: Defines Mode Adaptiveness, Tool Effect, NAAR, HCE, and the paper's central claims.
Figure 1 contrasts non-agentic, redundant tool use, and Beacon's adaptive and helpful tool use.
Figure 2 presents tool-call adaptiveness, the 13-benchmark average, and tool gain versus harm.
Motivates adaptive and effective tool use and positions Beacon against CodeDance, AdaTooler-V, Metis, and diagnostic studies.
Defines five-run text-easy/text-hard splitting, MAtext, MAtool, Tool-Gain, Tool-Harm, and diagnoses prior models.
Figure 3 compares tool-free/tool-available accuracy, Mode Adaptiveness, and Tool Effect.
Covers data construction, cold-start SFT, NAAR, HCE, hinted importance ratios, and the clipped GRPO objective.
Figure 4 illustrates normal, all-correct, and all-wrong group routing through NAAR and HCE.
Table 1 reports high-resolution search, spatial, and perceptual reasoning.
Table 2 reports quantitative, diagrammatic, compositional, and agentic reasoning; the asset is a verified manual recrop.
Table 3 gives per-dataset and average MA, Tool Effect, and Text-Retain metrics.
Table 4 compares GRPO, NAAR, HCE, and the full method.
Figure 5 shows training accuracy, adaptive reward, and format reward.
Figure 6 tracks response modes, adaptive labels, and mode-label alignment.
Figure 7 shows group composition and conversion of initially all-wrong groups.
Concludes that tool progress should be measured by necessity and genuine capability gain; retains 49 references in the source.
Provides the enforced-text prompt, VLMEvalKit settings, retries, tool-call cap, temperature, and Gemini semantic judgment.
Table 5 reports SFT and RL raw/retained counts.
Figure 8 maps task domains to public training sources.
Figure 9 shows task-category distributions for SFT and RL.
Figure 10 shows SFT per-source counts and retention.
Figure 11 shows RL per-source counts and retention.
Retains SFT synthesis/refinement protocols, SFT/RL hyperparameters, the shared autonomous-tool prompt, and hint-generation schema.
Table 6 expands the Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect ablation by dataset.
Documents forced-text reward collapse and provides three reasoning trajectories and three hint examples.
Tables 7-12 contain three tool-use trajectories and three answer-free hint examples.
